beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: While the devil starved the old world slowly, he took the other hemisphere by storm. The loneliest chapter in the whole war — and one of the bravest.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Remember what the Nephites had. The risen Christ had walked their streets. Watch what free people who choose him build: two hundred years of Zion — no poor, no classes, no war, all things common.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And surely there could not be a happier people among all the people who had been created by the hand of God.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Two centuries of the happiest people God ever made. The devil cannot force — so he sold them pride. Fine clothes. Classes. Grudges, renamed. And within living memory of paradise, his oldest franchise reopened: secret combinations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This is where the devil's road always goes. It ended at a hill called Cumorah — hundreds of thousands fell, the prophet-general Mormon with them. When the smoke cleared, one covenant keeper was left standing on the continent.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And my father also was killed by them, and I even remain alone to write the sad tale of the destruction of my people.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: I have not friends nor whither to go; and how long the Lord will suffer that I may live I know not.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Moroni. Son of Mormon. The last believer of a dead nation — hunted, homeless, carrying the one record the devil's editors never touched.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And what does the loneliest man in history do with the record of the people who broke his heart? He does not burn it. He finishes it — alone, for years — because your freedom to choose would one day hang on it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And in that farewell he does something astonishing. He writes to US — and explains how he can:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Behold, I speak unto you as if ye were present, and yet ye are not. But behold, Jesus Christ hath shown you unto me, and I know your doing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then he sealed the record, carried the plates to a hill the Lord showed him, and buried them in a stone box. The second witness — planted like a seed with a timer, addressed to a world that would one day need proof the heavens were never closed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The devil, watching, believed he now held both hemispheres. Keys gone in the east. A dead church, a dead nation, and a book in the ground in the west. Say his miscalculation with me one more time: a buried record is not a corpse. It is a seed.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And Moroni's last written words to you, before the dirt closed over the box, were an appointment:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: Ye shall see me at the bar of God; and the Lord God will say unto you: Did I not declare my words unto you, which were written by this man?

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: The last man of a dead nation wrote to you by firelight — and buried the letter where you would find it.
